plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, so bidding your true value maximizes your expected profit: bidding higher risks winning at a price above your value, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this holds for all rational bidders, I should bid exactly my value of $32.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy, regardless of other bidders' strategies or beliefs. This holds because: if I bid above value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth; if I bid below value, I risk losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my true value and my bid. Since my value is $6, I will bid exactly $6, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay the appropriate second-highest bid.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to you; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, regardless of Andy and Betty's strategies or beliefs about me, my optimal action is to bid exactly my private value of $17.
